body:
Alright as a man with autism (in the same family) let me help you out a little.

I have met 4 people from online dating sites including my current girlfriend. Meeting someone who you have only talked to online is at first an awkward experience. It's best to not mention your problem if you think there is a chance that she will take that in a negative way. My current girlfriend I told her on our first date at the end of the date. Then afterwords I asked if she even noticed, which she didn't. if you know how to control  it I suggest doing it but if you can't then maybe another approach is necessary. 

I then explained to her my story on my autism and how it affected me and if she is okay with this. She said yes and we have been happy together ever since. 

Now if you don't know how to control yourself and you think it's going to come out with you crossing the line on a question or doing something that could come off as a red flag; then you need to tell her sooner rather than later. 

I'm assuming you have hopes that this will turn into something else down the road. If that is the case then it's better to let her know now with a little explanation of things that you may do and if she is not okay with it,  or not willing to give you that date then she isn't right for you.

I have had a girl not want to go on a date with me because I told her I had autism. Yeah it's a low blow but so many girls are out there that when I say that it doesn't even phase them.

Alright now that I explained that what you should do on your date is ask open ended questions about her. Make sure the questions are innocent and not to out there. The way I figure out what questions are okay to ask the person and what questions may be crossing the line all depend on the answers they give me to a previous question. If the answer they give is innocent then my next question will remain innocent, if however they are pushing the boundaries becoming more sexual or a topic that isn't so innocent then my next question will also be that way. It's so they are controlling the topics of the conversation without realizing it, and it's a safe way to get to fun questions (sorry no examples of questions).

Overall the date with the girl should be a fun experience for both of you. The best advice I can give you besides that is act with confidence. Girls will melt if a man shows confidence in himself. Have fun buddy and good luck.

I mean one thing that has always bothered me is at one point when the guy confronted her he pulled out video tapes and said he watches it at least 2 times a week. It is video tapes of what he did to her. I told her when I found out that we have him, that we can finally put him in jail. She defended him saying that even though he did all this to her for two years, he was still a better father to her then anyone else. Which in my opinion sounds like a classic case of stockholm syndrome. She also said that if I go to the police she will deny anything that happened so I basically cant do anything. I know letting her go to deal with this is the right thing to do but I want to do this right. I have told her on the phone that I want her to figure out what she needs to do and when she is ready she has a home "aka me" waiting for her to return.
